messages:
ravi: RFC follow-up: proposal to crack router responsibilities into 'routing lanes' (fast, background, shard-bound) and pull decisioning into a tiny Arbiter service. Goal: eliminate accidental in-flight pinning during fails and make hard vs soft fallback explicit.

claire: +1 to separation. We should define precise semantics for three actions: PASS (route new requests to next variant), DRAIN (finish in-flight then stop assigning new), and FORCE (immediate routing + reject new old-variant binds).

ravi: agreed. Draft envelope for decisions: includes decision_id, rollout_id, tenant_id, action, drain_until, ttl, signer, version. Example below.

```json
{ "decision_id": "dec-2024-08-01-42", "rollout_id": "r-9876", "tenant_id": "t-42", "action": "DRAIN|PASS|FORCE", "drain_until": 1725550600, "ttl": 30, "signer": "arbiter-v1", "version": "1" }
```

dmitri: ops note: FORCE is dangerous w/ KV and streaming responses. We must never terminate mid-stream. FORCE should mean router refuses new binds to old variant and short-circuits new sessions; existing streams finish unless they exceed a failsafe. Also need a per-tenant 'max-active-requests' override so tenants with long tails aren't stuck.

linda: telemetry side: arbiter should require a stability window (e.g., 3 probes over 10m OR z-score beyond threshold) before upgrading action to FORCE. Keep manual overrides immediate.

ravi: + add a confidence_score and probe_count to envelope so routers can log why an action changed. Also include an optional reason string for operators.

deploy-bot: :rocket: scheduled staged rollout r-9876 cohort=canary1 @1725550012

ops-bot: alert: observed tail latency spike in canary1 @1725550035 (p90 1800ms)

claire: follow-up: migration path -> start arbiter opt-in per-tenant. Mirror arbiter decisions to the old controller API for 48h, collect diffs. Provide a CLI command to promote tenant to arbiter once mismatch rate < 0.5%.

dmitri: add offline-resilience: router caches last valid signed decision until ttl expires. If arbiter unreachable beyond a grace, router falls back to controller policy and emits an incident annotated with decision_miss_count.

linda: auditability: persist decision_id and signer in request traces. Make a queryable index for rollback forensics.

ravi: small protocol tweak: include api_version and rollback_hint (if applicable). Also recommend using JWT-signed decisions to avoid spoofing.

claire: toy curl example to fetch decisions from arbiter (for docs):

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARBITER_TOKEN" \
  https://arbiter.prod.internal/v1/decisions/tenant/t-42 | jq .
```

ravi: open questions: how to handle multi-variant A/B where traffic split is sticky? My thought: Arbiter publishes explicit split ratios and a cookie-namespace; router keeps local sticky mapping and can flush on DRAIN.

dmitri: propose per-variant cache-compat labels. Router refuses to mix variants with incompatible cache labels unless operator forces. This reduces inconsistent reads.

linda: metric hygiene: add a rollout_heartbeat metric from arbiter so we can detect silent failures.

ravi: next steps: I'll write a short RFC with: decision envelope proto, TTL/backup rules, migration checklist, operator playbooks (kill switches & verification queries). Will post for review next week.

claire: :thumbsup: please include rollback SLO impact analysis and sample config for per-tenant drain windows.

ravi: will do. Thanks team.
